title: Venison Stew
subtitle: Slow-braised venison with red wine and root vegetables
excerpt: Shoulder or haunch of venison braised slowly in red wine with juniper, thyme, and root vegetables until the meat is tender and the sauce is deep and gamey. A rich autumn and winter braise.

recipe.sourceNotes: Venison (deer meat) has been eaten in Britain since the Norman conquest, when deer parks were established as royal hunting grounds and venison was a prestige food reserved for the nobility. Today British farmed and wild venison — primarily red, roe, and fallow deer — is available year-round but is at its best in autumn and winter, when the flavour is deepest. Venison is leaner than beef, with very little intramuscular fat, which means it dries out quickly if overcooked on high heat. The solution is low, slow braising with sufficient liquid and the right flavourings to complement the natural gamey character of the meat. Juniper berries are the traditional spice pairing with game: they have a resinous, piney flavour that cuts the richness. Marinating the venison overnight in the red wine deepens the flavour and tenderises the meat slightly.

recipeTools.notes: A large, heavy casserole or saucepan with a lid that fits in the oven.

content.text: Venison shoulder must be braised at a low temperature for a long time: the collagen converts to gelatine over 2 to 2.5 hours, producing a silky, tender result. Check the liquid level every 30 minutes and top up with a little water or stock if needed. The venison is lean so it can dry out if the liquid reduces too much. The stew is significantly better on the second day after the flavours have had time to meld.

items.preparation: shoulder or haunch, cut into 4 cm pieces

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Season the venison. Heat the oil in a large, heavy casserole over high heat. Brown the venison in batches until deeply coloured. Remove and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Fry the onion and carrot for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato puree. Cook for 1 minute. Add the flour and stir to coat. Pour in the wine and stock, scraping up any brown bits. Add the juniper berries, thyme, bay, salt, and pepper. Return the venison.

Bring to a simmer, cover tightly, and transfer to the oven. Cook for 2 to 2.5 hours until the venison is very tender. Remove the thyme and bay. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve with mashed potato or celeriac mash.
